Angles written ∠ are read from the figure.

Plan: it suffices to show that H, A, K are collinear.

1. BH = BK and CH = CK, so BC is the perpendicular bisector of HK; hence BC ⟂ HK. (1)

2. AH ⟂ BC and HK ⟂ BC, by (1), so AH ∥ HK. (2)

3. AH ∥ HK, by (2), so H, A, K are collinear. (3)

4. We show that A, B, C, K lie on one circle:

∠C = ∠HBC − 90°    [BH ⟂ AC]
   = ∠BHK    [BC ⟂ HK, by (1)]
   = ∠HKB    [BH = BK]
   = ∠AKB    [H, A, K collinear, by (3)]

So A, B, C, K lie on one circle, as required. ∎
